content.comment_body: [product_name] [version_no] is not working with [product_name] [version_no], although the earlier [product_name] worked without issues. Looking for suggestions.

A couple of users in the German section reported this problem too. One of them contacted support. The response was: With [version_no], communication with [product_name] Professional Runtime or [product_name] flexible [version_no] isn’t possible. This was still supported with the older [product_name] [version_no]. If you want a definite answer, it’s recommended to open a support ticket.
Here is the reply from the support team, along with a Google Translate version.
Thanks for sharing; I’m facing the same problem with my [version_no] device.

Hello everyone, The issue is resolved in firmware [version_no], but the updated [product_name] is not available in the market yet. That’s the latest information from [company_name] support. It feels unreasonable to need to buy a new device since the current hardware can’t be updated via firmware.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing compatibility issues between [product_name] [version_no] hardware and [product_name] [version_no] software, whereas earlier hardware worked without problems. The latest hardware restricts communication with [product_name] Professional Runtime and [product_name] flexible [version_no], affecting standard workflows. Support from [company_name] confirms this limitation, stating that only newer devices will receive the necessary firmware update, leaving current users without a solution and leading to frustration.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] [version_no] hardware to continue supporting communication with [product_name] [version_no] software as previous hardware versions did, or at least have the option to update their current devices through a firmware release.
